contract: One MCP server that a tenant added at run time (Streamable HTTP, bearer token), turned into a ready integration/mcp-client runtime config only after three steps in fixed order: integration/egress-policy resolve/3 admits the https URL and every resolved address is public, else {:egress, reason} with egress-policy's own reason and nothing later runs; one integration/secrets resolution as the check before connecting, the value dropped, expired giving credentials_expired and any other failure or a raise, throw or exit of the secrets function giving credentials_unavailable; then Elzoo.McpClient.configure/1 with Elzoo.McpClient.RuntimeBinding and the egress host, port and whole checked address set (network :public), whose zero-arity credential Need resolves the reference again at each request. configure/1 takes exact keys, refuses a URL query and calls no Need. list_tools/2 keys the unchanged ready listing or unavailable{credentials_expired | credentials_unavailable | a finite reason of the ready client} by {tenant, server}, after the check. Tool calls stay the ready connect/2, admission/3, context/3 (bound to the admission's intent key, so a session of another runtime config, with another tenant, server text or URL, cannot execute an intent admitted under this one) and call_tool/3 path. Errors never echo the URL, host, token or reference; no telemetry or log of its own.
limits: Addresses are as fresh as the admission; after a disconnect the host admits again.

Redirect refusal and the response cap are ex_mcp and integration/mcp-client duties, held by ELZ-282's drift tests; the ELZ-282 loopback runtime tests are the transport evidence. This Piece cannot reach a loopback server through egress-policy, by design: a successful public connect is not exercised and there is no live public endpoint in the evidence.
One tenant credential per server; no per-person lists. No OAuth (Wave 9 integration/oauth-client), no stdio.
The check before the call and the credential Need are two samples of the Secrets resolver; a rotation between them is possible.

The pairing and the list_tools/2 match tie tenant, server text and URL only: configs that differ only in credential reference, addresses or bounds share the intent identity (so a config admitted again can recover an intent), and one credential per {tenant, server} is the host's duty.
The ready client's Adapter context is not opaque: host code that edits a context's session or key bypasses the pairing.
No claim about what a tool does. Finite tests; no proof is claimed.

grounding.claim: Named acceptance groups: egress_first (http, IP literal, non-allowlisted host, wrong port, nxdomain, resolver raise, 10.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1 and a mixed answer give egress-policy's reason with no secrets or Secrets resolver call and no client or socket), admission (exact host, port, sorted addresses, network and server; the Need resolves again on each call; a query, a forged policy struct and a URL over the ready 512-byte endpoint bound are configuration, invalid UTF-8 is egress malformed), credentials, keying (distinct {tenant, server} keys and rt1 identities for one ref; a session of another tenant, server text or URL, or a build-time session, is not listed), pairing (a session of another runtime config, with another tenant, server text or URL, cannot execute an intent admitted under this one, with a real delivery/effect-intent owner and the ready client's loopback server), secrecy, and the checked example; the credential-before-egress, first-address-only, server-only-key, URL-dropped-from-the-list_tools-match and any-policy-struct negative controls fail under temporary edits. Finite evidence, not proof.

ex_mcp 1.8.1 at its exact pin, reached only through the ready integration/mcp-client runtime mode, used unchanged with integration/egress-policy and integration/secrets; pinned-address transport, redirect refusal and the response cap are the ready client's, held by its drift tests.

The host supplies a truthful egress resolver that bounds its own time, a truthful secrets function and Secrets resolver with each scope bound to one tenant and one server, starts ex_mcp and a DynamicSupervisor, and supplies the recipient and owner of each tool call; the ready client's named assumption that a 401 or 403 means nothing ran.

telemetry.contract: No Elzoo event and no log of its own, as the ready client: ex_mcp emits upstream [:ex_mcp, ...] events and debug logs that consumer-installed handlers may see (the consumer's responsibility). Own events: a future task when a consumer needs them.

config.contract: Construction-time only through configure/1: tenant, server text, URL, egress policy and resolver Need, credential reference, secrets function and the ready client bounds with the ready ranges and defaults. No hot update; a changed URL, policy or credential is a new config, admitted again.

control.contract: The Piece owns no process; the host owns the session (Elzoo.McpClient.close/1). Dispatch and recovery of a tool call are the delivery/effect-intent owner's Control.
